claim: Once Object Lock is enabled on a bucket, you cannot disable Object Lock or Versioning for that bucket.
question: Can you turn off Object Lock after enabling it on a bucket?

values.display: cannot disable S3 Object Lock or S3 Versioning

evidence.quote: No, you cannot disable S3 Object Lock or S3 Versioning for buckets once S3 Object Lock is enabled.
After you enable Object Lock on a bucket, you can't disable Object Lock or suspend versioning for that bucket.

claim: To replicate objects from an Object Lock bucket, the destination bucket must also have Object Lock enabled.
question: Can a bucket with Object Lock be replicated, and what must the destination have?

values.display: destination bucket must also have S3 Object Lock enabled

evidence.quote: Additionally, to replicate objects from S3 Object Lock enabled buckets, your destination bucket must also have S3 Object Lock enabled.

claim: S3 Replication copies locked objects together with their retention metadata; replicated objects take the Object Lock configuration of the source bucket.
question: Is Object Lock retention copied to the replica?

evidence.quote: You can use Object Lock with S3 Replication to enable automatic, asynchronous copying of locked objects and their retention metadata, across S3 buckets. This means that for replicated objects, Amazon S3 takes the object lock configuration of the source bucket.

claim: Replicating from an Object Lock bucket needs the permissions s3:GetObjectRetention and s3:GetObjectLegalHold on the source bucket in the replication role; an s3:Get* permission also satisfies this.
question: What extra permissions does replication from an Object Lock bucket need?

evidence.quote: Yes, to replicate objects from S3 Object Lock enabled buckets you need to grant two new permissions, s3:GetObjectRetention and s3:GetObjectLegalHold, on the source bucket in the IAM role that you use to set up replication. Alternatively, if the IAM role has an s3:Get* permission, it satisfies the requirement.

claim: All replication features, including SRR, CRR, replication metrics, Replication Time Control and Batch Replication, are supported when replicating from Object Lock buckets.
question: Are any replication features unavailable for Object Lock buckets?

values.display: supported while replicating from S3 Object Lock buckets

evidence.quote: No, all features of S3 Replication, such as S3 Same-Region Replication (S3 SRR), S3 Cross-Region Replication (S3 CRR), S3 Replication metrics to track progress, S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC), and S3 Batch Replication, are supported while replicating from S3 Object Lock buckets.

claim: Object Lock supports broker-dealers who must keep records in a non-erasable, non-rewritable format under SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511 or CFTC Regulation 1.31.
question: Which financial regulations does AWS cite for S3 Object Lock?

values.display: SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511, or CFTC Regulation 1.31

evidence.quote: For customers in the financial services industry, S3 Object Lock provides added support for broker-dealers who must retain records in a non-erasable and non-rewritable format to satisfy regulatory requirements of SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511, or CFTC Regulation 1.31.

claim: For these financial-services record rules, AWS is not a designated third party (D3P); you must select a D3P yourself and name it in the notification to your regulator.
question: Is AWS the designated third party for SEC and CFTC record-keeping?

evidence.quote: For the purposes of these requirements, AWS is not a designated third party (D3P). Be sure to select a D3P and include this information in your notification to your DEA.

claim: For changing, unpredictable or unknown access patterns, AWS says S3 Intelligent-Tiering should be the default storage class.
question: Which storage class does AWS recommend when the access pattern is unknown?

values.display: should be the default storage class

evidence.quote: Many workloads have changing (user-generated content), unpredictable (analytics, data lakes), or unknown (new applications) access patterns, and that is why S3 Intelligent-Tiering should be the default storage class to automatically save on storage costs.

claim: S3 Standard is the best choice when you access data more than once a month; S3 Standard-IA suits data kept for at least a month and accessed once every month or two.
question: At what access frequency does AWS draw the line between S3 Standard and S3 Standard-IA?

evidence.quote: The S3 Standard storage class is ideal for frequently accessed data; this is the best choice if you access data more than once a month. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access is ideal for data retained for at least a month and accessed once every month or two.

claim: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects not accessed for 30 consecutive days to the Infrequent Access tier (up to 40% saving) and after 90 days of no access to the Archive Instant Access tier (up to 68%).
question: After how many days without access does Intelligent-Tiering move an object down a tier?

evidence.quote: For a low monthly object monitoring and automation charge, S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects that have not been accessed for 30 consecutive days to the Infrequent Access tier to save up to 40% on storage costs. After 90 days consecutive days of no access, objects are moved to the Archive Instant Access tier to save up to 68% on storage costs.

claim: With the optional archive tiers enabled, objects not accessed for a minimum of 90 days move to the Archive Access tier (up to 71% saving) and after 180 days to the Deep Archive Access tier (up to 95%).
question: When do Intelligent-Tiering objects move into the optional Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers?

evidence.quote: Once you enable one or both of the asynchronous archive access tiers, S3 Intelligent-Tiering will move objects that have not been accessed for a minimum of 90 days to the Archive Access tier to save up to 71% and after 180 days of no access to the Deep Archive Access tier to save up to 95% for rarely accessed objects.

claim: An object in the Infrequent Access or Archive Instant Access tier that is accessed later is moved back to the Frequent Access tier automatically.
question: What happens when a tiered-down Intelligent-Tiering object is read again?

values.display: automatically moved back to the Frequent Access tier

evidence.quote: If an object in the Infrequent Access tier or Archive Instant Access tier is accessed later, it is automatically moved back to the Frequent Access tier.

claim: There are no retrieval charges in S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and no tiering or lifecycle charges when objects move between its access tiers.
question: Does Intelligent-Tiering charge retrieval fees?

evidence.quote: There are no retrieval charges in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. No additional tiering or lifecycle charges apply when objects are moved between access tiers within the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.

claim: Intelligent-Tiering charges a small monthly monitoring and automation fee per object, in addition to storage, requests and data transfer.
question: What does Intelligent-Tiering charge that other classes do not?

evidence.quote: S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges you for monthly storage, requests, and data transfer, and charges a small monthly charge for monitoring and automation per object.

claim: S3 Intelligent-Tiering has no minimum storage duration.
question: Is there a minimum storage duration for Intelligent-Tiering?

evidence.quote: No. The S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class has no minimum storage duration.

claim: Intelligent-Tiering has no minimum billable object size, but objects smaller than 128KB are not eligible for auto-tiering: they are always charged at Frequent Access rates with no monitoring and automation charge.
question: How does Intelligent-Tiering treat objects smaller than 128KB?

qualifiers.scope: per object, S3 Intelligent-Tiering auto-tiering threshold

evidence.quote: No. The S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class has no minimum billable object size, but objects smaller than 128KB are not eligible for auto-tiering. These smaller objects will always be charged at the Frequent Access tier rates, with no monitoring and automation charge.

claim: Objects in the Archive Access tier return to the Frequent Access tier in 3-5 hours, and within 12 hours from the Deep Archive Access tier, after a Restore request.
question: How long does a restore from the Intelligent-Tiering archive tiers take?

evidence.quote: To access an object in the Archive or Deep Archive Access tiers, you need to issue a Restore request and the object will begin moving back to the Frequent Access tier, all within the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Objects in the Archive Access Tier are moved to the Frequent Access tier in 3-5 hours, objects in the Deep Archive Access tier are moved to the Frequent Access tier within 12 hours.

claim: You can lifecycle objects out of S3 Intelligent-Tiering to S3 One Zone-IA, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
question: Can Lifecycle move objects from Intelligent-Tiering to another class?

values.display: S3 One-Zone Infrequent Access, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive

evidence.quote: Yes. You can lifecycle objects from S3 Intelligent-Tiering Frequent Access, Infrequent, and Archive Instant Access tiers to S3 One-Zone Infrequent Access, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

claim: Intelligent-Tiering is designed for 99.9% availability and 99.999999999% durability, with the same latency and throughput as S3 Standard.
question: What availability and durability is Intelligent-Tiering designed for?

evidence.quote: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is designed for 99.9% availability and 99.999999999% durability, and automatically offers the same low latency and high throughput performance of S3 Standard.

claim: Data deleted from S3 Standard-IA within 30 days is charged for the full 30 days.
question: What is the minimum storage duration charge for S3 Standard-IA?

evidence.quote: Data that is deleted from S3 Standard-IA within 30 days will be charged for a full 30 days.

claim: S3 Standard-IA has a minimum object storage charge of 128KB; smaller objects are charged as if they were 128KB.
question: What is the minimum billable object size in S3 Standard-IA?

evidence.quote: S3 Standard-IA is designed for larger objects and has a minimum object storage charge of 128KB. Objects smaller than 128KB in size will incur storage charges as if the object were 128KB.

claim: S3 Standard-IA combines a low per-GB storage price with a per-GB retrieval charge, and keeps the durability, throughput and low latency of S3 Standard.
question: What does S3 Standard-IA charge that S3 Standard does not?

evidence.quote: S3 Standard-IA offers the high durability, throughput, and low latency of the Amazon S3 Standard storage class, with a low per-GB storage price and per-GB retrieval charge.

claim: Lifecycle policies can tier objects from S3 Standard-IA to S3 One Zone-IA, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
question: Can Lifecycle move objects from S3 Standard-IA to colder classes?

values.display: from S3 Standard-IA to S3 One Zone-IA

evidence.quote: Yes. In addition to using Lifecycle policies to migrate objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA, you can also set up Lifecycle policies to tier objects from S3 Standard-IA to S3 One Zone-IA, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.

claim: Changing an object from S3 Standard-IA to S3 Standard with a COPY request incurs an S3 Standard COPY request charge and an S3 Standard-IA data retrieval charge.
question: What does it cost to move an object back from S3 Standard-IA to S3 Standard?

evidence.quote: You will incur charges for an S3 Standard (destination storage class) COPY request and an S3 Standard-IA (source storage class) data retrieval.

claim: S3 One Zone-IA stores data redundantly within a single Availability Zone at 20% less cost than S3 Standard-IA.
question: How much cheaper is S3 One Zone-IA than S3 Standard-IA?

evidence.quote: S3 One Zone-IA storage redundantly stores data within that single Availability Zone to deliver storage at 20% less cost than geographically redundant S3 Standard-IA storage, which stores data redundantly across multiple geographically separate Availability Zones.

claim: S3 One Zone-IA suits infrequently accessed backup copies, disaster recovery copies or other easily re-creatable data.
question: What kind of data belongs in S3 One Zone-IA?

evidence.quote: Customers can use S3 One Zone-IA for infrequently-accessed storage, like backup copies, disaster recovery copies, or other easily re-creatable data.
